test_title: PYST 64: RRB Group D - Mathematics (Held On: 26 Dec, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: maths
question: One pipe can fill a tank in 6 minutes, while another pipe can empty the completely filled tank in 12 minutes. If both the pipes are opened together when the tank is empty, how many minutes will it take to fill one-half of the tank?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

If an inlet pipe fills a tank in x minutes and an outlet empties it in y minutes, time to fill the full tank = (x × y) ÷ (y − x).

Time for full tank = (6 × 12) ÷ (12 − 6) = 72 ÷ 6 = 12 minutes.

Time required to fill one-half of the tank = 12 ÷ 2 = 6 minutes.

**∴ The correct answer is 6 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by filling pipe = 6 minutes

Time taken by emptying pipe = 12 minutes

**Calculations:**

 
 

 **Pipe**
 **Minutes**
 **Total Work**
 **Efficiency**
 
 

 Filling Pipe
 6
 12
 2
 
 

 Emptying Pipe
 12
 −1
 
 

⇒ Net efficiency when both pipes are opened = 2 − 1 = 1 unit/minute

⇒ Total capacity of the tank = 12 units

⇒ Capacity to be filled (one-half of the tank) = 12 ÷ 2 = 6 units

⇒ Time required to fill half the tank = Work ÷ Net Efficiency

⇒ Time required = 6 ÷ 1 = 6 minutes

**∴ The correct answer is 6 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Inlet and Outlet Pipes

An inlet pipe adds water to the tank, so its work (efficiency) is considered positive (+). An outlet pipe drains water, so its work is considered negative (−).

Capacity of the Tank

Capacity = Time taken by a pipe × Efficiency of that pipe. For ease of calculation, the total capacity is always taken as the LCM of all given time values.

Pipes operating on Alternate Minutes

If an inlet and an outlet are opened in alternate minutes, calculate cycles until the tank is nearly full. Stop the cycle right before the inlet completely fills the tank to prevent the outlet from emptying an already full tank.
